G1909.as:

with primary sense of superposition, on, upon.
I. C. gen.,
1. of place, answering the question, where?
(a) of the place on which, on, upon: ἐπὶ (τ.) γῆς, , , al.; τ. κεφαλῆς, ; τ. νεφελῶν, , al.; like ἐν, in constr. praegn. after verbs of motion: βάλλειν, ; σπείρειν, ; ἔρχεσθαι, , al.; fig., ἐπ’ ἀληθείας (MM, s.v. ἀ.); of the subject of thought or speech, ; of power or authority, over, πάντων, : τ. γάζης, ; ἐξουσία, ;
(b) of vicinity, at, by: τ. θαλάσσης, ; τ. ὁδοῦ, ; τοῦ βάτου, (v. Swete, in l.); c. gen. pers., in the presence of, before, , , , al.
2. Of time,

(b) c. gen. rei, at, at the time of: , , ; ἐπὶ τ. προσευχῶν, , , , .
II. C. dat., of place, answering the question, where?
(a) lit., on, upon: , , al.; after verbs of motion (v. supr., I, 1, (a)), ; above, ; at, by, , , , al.;
(b) metaph., upon, on the ground of, (LXX); in the matter of, (v. Swete, in l.); upon, of, concerning, , ; of the ground, reason or motive (Bl., §38, 2; 43, 3), , , al.; ἐφ’ ᾧ, for the reason that, because, ; after verbs of motion, over, , , al.; of a condition (cl.), , ; ἐπὶ δυσὶ μάρτυσιν (v. Westc. on ), ; of purpose or aim, , ; of authority, over, ; of hostility, c. dat. pers. (cl.), against, ; in addition to (cl.), ; of an adjunct, in, at, on, .
III. C. acc.,
1. of place of motion upon or over, answering the question, whither?
(a) lit., upon, over: , , , al. mult.; in NT also, answering the question, where? (as c. gen., dat.), , , ; ἐπὶ τ. αὐτό, , al.; of motion to a vicinity, to, , , al.;
(b) metaph. (in wh. "the acc. is more widely prevalent than it strictly should be," Bl., §43, 1); of blessings, evils, etc., coming upon one, c. acc. pers., , , , , al.; of addition (dat. in cl.), λύπη ἐπὶ λύπην, ; ἐπικαλεῖν ὄνομα ἐπί (v.s. ἐπικαλέω), , ; καλεῖν ἐπί, to call after, ; of number or degree: ἐπὶ τρίς (cl. εἰς τ.), thrice, ; ἐπὶ πλεῖον, the more, further, (v. also infr., 2, (a)); ἐφ’ ὅσον (v. infr., ib.), forasmuch as, , , ; of power, authority, control, , , , al.; of the direction of thoughts and feelings, unto, towards, , , , , , , , al.; of purpose, for, , ; ἐφ’ ὅ πάρει (Rec. ἐφ’ ᾧ, ; of hostility, against, , , , , , , ; Of reference, concerning, for (cl. usually dat.), , , .
2. Of time,
(a) during, for: (WH, txt., omits ἐπί), , , al.; ἐφ’ ὅσον (χρόνον), as long as, for so long time as, , al. (for ἐφ’ ὅ in another sense, v. supr., 1, (b)); ἐφ’ ἱκανόν (v.s. ἱ), ; ἐπὶ πλεῖον (v. supr., 1, (b)), yet longer, further, ;
(b) on, about, towards (cl. εἰς): .
IV. In composition, ἐπί signifies: up, ἐπαίρω; upon, ἐπίγειος, ἐπιδημέω, ἐπικαθίζω; towards, επιβλέπω, ἐπεκτείνω; over (of superintendence), ἐπιστάτης; again, in addition, ἐπαιτέω; against, ἐπιορκέω, ἐπιβουλή.

G1967.as:
*† ἐπιούσιος, -ον (cf. περιούσιος, [in LXX for סְגֻלָּה, De 7:6, etc.]),
found only in the phrase ἄρτος ἐ., EV, daily; R, mg., for the coming day: , . (Several derivations find support, each pointing to a different meaning.
1. < ἐπιοῦσα (sc. ἡμέρα) (or, < ἐπὶ τὴν ἰοῦσαν (sc. ήμέραν), Zorell, s.v.), hence, for the morrow or for the coming day (R, mg.).
2.
(a) < ἐπί + οὐσία, hence, for subsistence, needful (Am. R, mg.);
(b) < ἐπί + εἶναι in fem. ptcp. form, hence, pertaining to (the day). For renderings of versions and views of various writers, v. reff. in DB, ext., 36 f.; DCG, ii, 58 f., 62a; ICC on Lk, l.c. The EV, daily, is based on the Vg. (Lk; OL, Mt, Lk, quotidianus). "It is difficult not to think that τὸν ἐ. rests upon misunderstanding of an original Aramaic phrase, or upon a Greek corruption" (ICC on Mt, l.c.; cf. also Cremer, 239).†
